claims.text: The starting FeCoNi alloy or high-entropy derivative is single-phase FCC.
FeCoNi or a high-entropy derivative has high saturation magnetization.
The starting material has a coercive field below 100 Oe.
Refining grains into the nanocrystalline regime near the single-domain size will increase coercivity relative to a coarse-grained material.
Grain refinement to near or below the single-domain size will increase coercivity at room temperature.
Nanostructuring will largely preserve the saturation magnetization.
High-energy ball milling followed by tuned annealing can produce nanocrystalline grains while preserving the single FCC phase.
Decreasing particle or grain size increases coercivity until the single-domain size is reached.
Grain refinement creates a larger population of single-domain grains.
Single-domain nanocrystalline grains have increased magnetic-anisotropy barriers that hinder domain-wall motion.
Near the single-domain size, magnetization reversal by domain-wall motion is suppressed.
Coherent rotation replaces domain-wall motion as the dominant reversal mechanism near the single-domain size.
The energy barrier for coherent rotation or reversed-domain nucleation produces a higher coercive field.
The intervention will raise coercivity from below 100 Oe to several times the baseline value.
The intervention is bounded to samples that remain single-phase FCC without chemical segregation, oxidation, or impurity phases.
A sample remaining below 100 Oe after nanostructuring would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction is a several-fold increase relative to baseline, but the falsification rule uses an absolute 100 Oe threshold. A several-fold increase from a sufficiently low baseline could remain below 100 Oe and simultaneously satisfy the prediction and trigger falsification.

The hypothesis is explicitly restricted to processing that retains single-phase FCC, yet transformation away from FCC is treated as falsification rather than as failure to implement the specified intervention.
